tasks.short: Pick up the work order, read it and the instructions, talk with the supervisor or homeowner on site about requirements, and get missing details from the office.

steps.what: Painter picks up paper work orders at the office
Painter reads work orders to determine work requirements
Painter receives instructions from supervisors or homeowners on site
Painter phones the office for missing details

tasks.design: Work orders arrive on the painter's phone in the site app ({OPS_SYSTEM}) with address, colours, surfaces and photos from the estimate visit, so the painter no longer collects paper at the office and phones less for missing details. Reading the order and agreeing details with the homeowner on site stay with the painter.
tasks.previous_blocker: Work orders were paper and details came by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Mobile work orders with photos are standard in site apps.
tasks.still_hard: Homeowners change their minds on site.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what a homeowner really wants behind 'just a fresh white'.

reach.learn: Whether fewer calls come from site.

evidence.claim: At RRS in Enschede, about 200 handhelds replaced paper work orders; technicians had spent half an hour a day on hold for their next job.
Hours, location and job logs per worker need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the planned job to details completed; the painting is outside.
Input contract: estimate details and photos entered by the office; fallback is paper and phone.
Reading and agreeing on site do not change.
research_questions: Do calls to the office fall?

incremental.description: Painter adds site photos to the work order.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: long jobs with one work order, where the painter passes the office anyway and details are often missing (9.0); high: many short jobs a week with complete estimate details (22.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Measure surfaces, calculate paint and material amounts, price materials and labour, check the estimate, and send it to the customer.

steps.what: Painter calculates amounts of required materials by hand
Painter estimates costs of materials and labour in a spreadsheet
Painter checks the estimate: surfaces, coats, products and hours fit what was seen on site, and it is for this customer
Painter sends the checked estimate to the customer: by e-mail today, by one send from the estimate app after the change

tasks.design: A laser meter sends measurements to the estimate app ({OTHER}), which computes areas, litres per coat from the product's spread rate, and prices materials from the supplier's price data and labour from the firm's rates. The painter checks the estimate and sends it to the customer from the app. Measuring and judging the surfaces stay with the painter.
tasks.previous_blocker: Measurements were written down and paint and costs worked out by hand or in a spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Laser meters connect to estimate apps that hold supplier prices.
tasks.still_hard: Surface condition changes the work more than the area does.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that old woodwork needs stripping, not just a coat.
tasks.altitude: The painter checks estimates instead of computing them.

reach.learn: Whether quotes go out the same day.

evidence.claim: 2BA is a product and price data hub that installer software connects to.
Laser meters can send measurements to estimate apps by Bluetooth.

assumptions: Boundary: from the estimate visit to the estimate sent; contract signing is outside.
Input contract: spread rates and prices from suppliers; labour rates set by the firm; fallback is hand calculation.
Measuring stays with the painter; s1 keeps 80 because only noting readings goes. The check keeps its full time and s5 keeps 20 for the send.
Customers read the estimate as before; no added customer time.
research_questions: Do material shortages on jobs fall?

incremental.description: Painter checks product spread rates in the app.

approvals.approved_version: The estimate with surfaces, materials, labour and prices exactly as checked by the painter in s4, sent once from the estimate app to the customer's address; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a few large jobs with unusual surfaces and products outside the price data, so many amounts and prices are still worked out by hand (35.5); high: many small standard estimates (50.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Discuss finishes and colours with the customer, compare products for durability and application, decide the products, order them, and collect them.

steps.what: Painter discusses finishes and colours with the customer
Painter compares tools and finishes for durability, ease of handling and methods of application
Painter selects tools and finishes for the surfaces
Painter checks the order before it is placed: products, amounts, the firm's account and the delivery address and date
Painter places the checked order: by phone at the supplier today, in the supplier's trade app for delivery to site after the change
Painter collects the products at the supplier's shop

tasks.design: Product data sheets with durability, drying times and application methods show in the supplier's trade app ({ECOMMERCE}) next to the firm's account prices, so the painter compares products without phoning the shop. Once the painter has chosen and checked the order, it is placed in the same app for delivery to site, which cuts trips to the shop. Talking with the customer and choosing products stay with the painter.
tasks.previous_blocker: Products were compared from memory and phone calls, and collected at the shop.
tasks.enabler_now: Supplier trade apps show data sheets and take orders for site delivery.
tasks.still_hard: Colour matching often needs a sample in hand.
tasks.human_edge: Advising a finish that will still look good after ten winters.

reach.learn: Whether site deliveries replace shop pickups.

evidence.claim: 2BA is a product and price data hub that trade software connects to.

assumptions: Boundary: from customer wishes to products on site; painting is outside.
Input contract: supplier app with the firm's account; fallback is phone and shop.

Talking with customers, choosing products and the order check keep their full time. s2 keeps 70 because data sheets sit side by side but are still read. s4 keeps 50 for building the order in the app. s5 keeps 50 for items still collected.
Suppliers deliver to site at no extra time for the painter.
research_questions: Do trips to the shop fall?

incremental.description: Painter checks site deliveries against the order.

approvals.approved_version: The order with products and amounts exactly as checked by the painter in s3c, placed once on the firm's account in the supplier's trade app for delivery to the named site; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the supplier's shop is next to the yard, so few trips are saved (15.0); high: jobs far from the shop (19.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The painter keeps reading jobs, talking with customers, measuring and choosing products; paper orders, hand calculations and shop trips shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using the estimate and trade apps
role.ambitious_version: A painter with more time on the brush.
